title: Ulla bar Rav

paragraphs: He served as a synagogue prayer leader in Rava’s time. In [Pesachim 117b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.117b.17) he led the service before Rava, used the wording of the elders of Pumbedita, and Rava said nothing to him.
In [Yoma 87b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.87b.11) [Hyman cites 67a], he led the service before Rava, beginning with “You chose us” and concluding with “What are we?” Rava praised him.
In [Megillah 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.21b.17), he poses a question to Rava, and at [24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.24b.2-3) he poses a question to Abaye.[^4]

notes.text: The complete prayer passage is Yoma87b, while the notice cites67a. Rava praises Ulla for the prayer formulation; ושבחיה does not mean and his praise. The locator mismatch remains open.

No new whole primary scalar was supplied here. The earlier complete Yoma 87b consultation is inherited beside supplied סז. (67a); no new whole-folio 67a absence claim is made. נחית קמיה describes leading prayer before Rava, and ושבחיה means he praised him, not and his praise. The prayer openings and Rava's silence in the Pesachim notice remain as supplied; no permanent appointment or geographical descent is inferred. Megillah's two addressees remain Rava and Abaye, respectively.

The printed notice cites 67a. Yoma 87b names Ulla bar Rav as leading Ne’ilah before Rava and gives the fuller ending “What are we, what are our lives?” Rava praises him there. In Pesachim 117b, Rava remains silent. Megillah 21b names Rava as the recipient of Ulla’s question about the New Moon reading, and 24b names Abaye as the recipient of his question about a minor reading Torah with limbs exposed.

[Pesachim 117b:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.117b.17) reports Rava’s silence. [Yoma 87b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.87b.11) reports his praise after Ulla led Ne’ilah. The corresponding [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2853&lang=en) gives 87b and lists both Megillah questions.
